text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended little changed in afternoon trade. Traders said activity was restricted by lack of fresh fundamental news and the Independence holiday in New York. September, the London benchmark, drifted within a $15 band to finish the day unchanged at $1,795 a tonne. Other months ended unchanged to $5.00 lower. Dealers expect that trading will stay subdued until New York reopens on Monday afternoon.

COLOMBIA - Colombia cut its internal coffee price by 10.17 per cent on July 5 in the seventh such reduction since a new sliding scale formula was introduced to adjust prices paid to growers on January 31, the National Coffee Growers' Federation said. It said the new price, effective until July 12, had been set at 339.875 pesos per 125-kg load. The cut was one of the sharpest since mid-June when the internal price was trimmed by 11.6 per cent.

UNITED STATES - For the week ended June 28, roastings totalled approximately 290,000 60-kg bags, unchanged from the previous week and compared with 280,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage reported. Cumulative roastings so far totalled 8.635 million 60- bags vs 8.395 million bags in the same year-ago period.

BRAZIL - The country's coffee regions should see no damaging cold until July 13, with temperatures rising throughout the week, local weather forecast Somar said. A polar air mass which passed swiftly through the south of the country over the weekend led to cooler weather but lows in north Parana, the most southern coffee growing region, were 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, it was added. Temperatures will take up until July 13, with a second air mass which is to pass quickly through the far south of the country at the start of the week staying well clear off coffee regions.

KENYA - Kenya has suspended its weekly coffee export auctions for the next two weeks because of acute shortages, a senior official at the Coffee Board of Kenya said. Auctions will resume on July 22. Drought that ravaged most growing areas of East Africa from October last year and persisted to March had forced a severe cut in coffee production and coffee reaching the market from farmers was well below earlier predictions, the CBK said. A trader from a leading coffee trade house in Nairobi said that coffee from the mid fly crop was forecast at just between 330,000 to 415,000 60-kg bags. The CBK 1996/97 (October/September) production figure of 1.308 million bags compares to 1.630 million bags in 1995/96 and 1.597 million bags in 1994/95.

CZECH REPUBLIC ** - Coffee imports in April 1997 amounted to 66,200 bags, up from 55,700 bags in March 1997. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1997 up to 239,800 bags. Major countries of origin in the first four months of 1997 were Vietnam with 34,600 bags green coffee, Brazil with 32,800 bags and Tanzania with 24,800 bags. The largest suppliers of solubles were Poland (13,100 bags) and Germany (12,500 bags).
